text:
A: Hello, hello! Joanne, is it? Can you hear me alright?
B: Yes. Hello. Sorry, my screen froze for a second.
A: No worries, you're here now. I'm Darren. Where are you calling from?
B: Crawley.
A: Crawley, so right by Gatwick. I'm Basingstoke. What do you do, then?
B: Erm, nothing at the moment. I was in accounts, purchase ledger, at a builders' merchants near Gatwick. Seventeen years. I was made redundant last year.
A: You're joking. Builders' merchants? That's me! I'm branch manager at one: yard, trade counter, the lot. Which lot were you with?
B: Erm, I'd rather not say, really. They got bought out anyway, and the back office went up to Milton Keynes.
A: Yeah, that's happening all over. Head office loves a centralise. Seventeen years though, that's rough.
B: It was a bit of a shock, yeah.
A: I'll tell you what, I could do with someone like you. I'm hopeless on the paperwork side. My assistant manager does all of it: rotas, compliance, stock audits. I leave my reports till the night before, right, and then it's panic stations.
B: Supplier statements were the worst. Reconciling them at month end.
A: Oh, don't. We had a rep take me out for a steak lunch the other week, lovely, all very friendly. Then his invoice comes in and the pricing's nothing like what we'd agreed over the steak. So I'm on the phone going, mate, I bought dessert on the strength of that.
B: Erm, that happens a lot. The credit notes never match either.
A: Never! They never match. So are you looking for something similar?
B: Sort of. Admin, part-time, something local. Not on the phones, ideally.
A: Not phones, yeah, fair enough. My trade counter would eat you alive. Good lads, but they'll shout at you because their copper fittings are late.
B: That's the bit I don't want, really.
A: Anyway, yeah. I saw the Jack Russell photo on your wall.
B: Oh. That's Bobby. He's fourteen now. His back leg's playing up, and the vet bills are, erm, a lot.
A: Don't talk to me about vets. Murphy, my Lab, ate a whole tea towel last week. Two hundred quid.
B: A whole one?
A: The whole thing. And it came out the other end, well, I won't go into that.
B: Bobby ate a sock once.
A: They're all the same. Do you walk him much?
B: Tilgate Park, every morning. Same route.
A: Lovely. I do Murphy at weekends, mostly. Nicola does the week and she reckons I owe her. Did you do the puzzle bit?
B: Yes. I liked that, actually.
A: You'd be the one. I guessed half of mine. And the bloke on my last call finished his and all, so I'm surrounded by clever people today.
B: It was just patterns, really.
A: Just patterns, she says. Right, well, if they ever want someone to do the paperwork for this study, I know who I'm—
